source_excerpt: The volume of the cortex, including the hippocampus, amounts to about 87 mm³ in one hemisphere.
extraction_note: Whole cortex including hippocampus, ONE hemisphere; not neocortex. Fig. 80 (p. 186) summarises the same figure as 2 x 87 mm³ (iso- and allocortex).

source_excerpt: If only the volume of the neocortex is considered which is 56 mm³ in one hemisphere
extraction_note: Neocortex, ONE hemisphere. Zhang & Sejnowski 2000 give G = 112 mm³, i.e. 2 x 56 mm³ (both hemispheres); the doubling is theirs and 112 is not printed in the book.

source_locus: Chapter 31 (Map of the Cortex), "Thickness of the Cortex"
source_excerpt: the average of the whole cortex, except for the hippocampus and fascia dentata, can be computed as 0.65 mm (on paraffin embedded material)
extraction_note: Area-weighted average over sectors of the cortical map, measured on paraffin sections (shrunken tissue); excludes hippocampus and fascia dentata. Local values are in Fig. 72 (p. 167, not extracted).

source_locus: Chapter 31 (Map of the Cortex), "Thickness of the Cortex"
source_excerpt: The unfixed mouse cortex should have an average thickness between 0.8 and 0.9 mm.
extraction_note: Authors' shrinkage-corrected estimate, not a direct measurement. Source of Zhang & Sejnowski 2000 Sect. 4 (0.8-0.9 mm); Zhang use the midpoint T = 0.85 mm in Sect. 8.

source_locus: Chapter 4 (Density of Neurons), text (sentence runs from p. 25 to p. 27; p. 26 holds Figs. 11-12)
source_excerpt: The figure of about 10⁵ per square millimetre corresponds to that given by Rockel et al. (1980).
extraction_note: Order-of-magnitude summary of the counts in Fig. 12 (areas 8, 6 and 17 of three mice; Schüz and Palm, 1989). Rockel et al. (1980) is a comparison, not the source. Zhang & Sejnowski 2000 Sect. 8 cite refs 22, 28 and 30 for neuron density per unit area of this order.
